newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: World Bank Kazakh loans to top $1.2 bln by end-'97.
newsitem.headline: World Bank Kazakh loans to top $1.2 bln by end-'97.

text.p: Total World Bank loans to Kazakhstan will exceed $1.2 billion by the end of 1997, including a $230 million loan now being negotiated, the bank's resident representative in the Central Asian state said late on Thursday.
David Pearce told a news conference that starting from 1993 the World Bank had approved 13 loans for Kazakhstan worth a total of $958.6 million.
"This week in Washington a loan of $230 million to Kazakhstan is being negotiated before the approval which we expect in August," Pearce said.

He said the new loan -- for public sector resource management -- would be a further boost for Kazakhstan's market reforms, and the first tranche worth $80 million could be disbursed straight after the approval of the loan.
"Besides, we are working actively on three additional loans, two of which, we hope, will be approved towards the end of this year," Pearce said.

He said one of the loans, worth $120 million, would be channelled to improve roads in several regions of Kazakhstan, another $60 million would go to support private farming, and $10 million to help the country's legal reform.
Pearce said the total amount of loans to be approved by the World Bank for Kazakhstan this year would exceed $400 million.
He said Kazakhstan ranks third among members of the Commonwealth of Independent States -- following Russia and Ukraine -- according to the amount of loans granted by the World Bank so far.
